reference: pvlib-python (NREL SPA, Ineichen-Perez clear sky, Perez 1990 transposition, Erbs decomposition, Kasten-Young air mass, Martin-Ruiz IAM, Faiman cell temperature) plus closed-form projected areas and diffuse view factors derived and implemented independently in this file
citations: I. Reda and A. Andreas, "Solar Position Algorithm for Solar Radiation Applications", NREL/TP-560-34302, rev. January 2008 - verification example of Appendix A.5
P. Ineichen and R. Perez, "A new airmass independent formulation for the Linke turbidity coefficient", Solar Energy 73(3):151-157, 2002
R. Perez et al., "Modeling daylight availability and irradiance components from direct and global irradiance", Solar Energy 44(5):271-289, 1990 (coefficient set of Table 6)
D.G. Erbs, S.A. Klein, J.A. Duffie, "Estimation of the diffuse radiation fraction for hourly, daily and monthly-average global radiation", Solar Energy 28(4):293-302, 1982
F. Kasten and A.T. Young, "Revised optical air mass tables and approximation formula", Applied Optics 28(22):4735-4738, 1989
N. Martin and J.M. Ruiz, "Calculation of the PV modules angular losses under field conditions by means of an analytical model", Solar Energy Materials & Solar Cells 70(1):25-38, 2001

J.A. Duffie and W.A. Beckman, "Solar Engineering of Thermal Processes", 4th ed., Wiley 2013 - angular dependence of absorptance of flat-black paint (7th-order fit) and the Brandemuehl-Beckman effective incidence angles for sky- and ground-diffuse
D. Faiman, "Assessing the outdoor operating temperature of photovoltaic modules", Progress in Photovoltaics 16(4):307-315, 2008

W. Holtzclaw / NOAA ESRL Global Monitoring Laboratory Solar Calculator, based on J. Meeus, "Astronomical Algorithms", 2nd ed., Willmann-Bell 1998 - the low-precision solar position algorithm the tool implements
